auto_bpm_transition.name: auto_bpm_transition
evidence: Local test (HTTP, build 18.0.9598, 2026-09-07, tools/probe_bpm_transition.py, two runs with the form order reversed, artifact tests/bpm-transition-forms.json): with a 100 BPM track on deck 1, a 120 BPM track on deck 2 pitched to 132, both decks stopped, the pair settles on a landing BPM that depends on the tail. Bare and both nonsense controls land on 120 (the target's ORIGINAL BPM) — so that is the default. 'source_original' lands on 100 and 'target_current' on 132, neither of which anything else reaches, so both are confirmed. 'target_current' is the only form that leaves the transition still engaged afterwards (query stays yes); every other form disengages. 'all' lands on 132 like 'target_current' but disengages. 'target_original' lands on 120, the same as bare and as the controls, so this observable cannot separate it from an ignored tail — it names the default; retested with smart_play off, where the default is still 120. Earlier probes reported these tokens as junk because their observable was the boolean 'is a transition running', which cannot see which BPM it targets. The verb is a TOGGLE: a second execute while one is running stops it, which is how an in-run form silently measured nothing until the prober started waiting for disengagement.
Kind from the vtable override matrix (tests/action-contracts.json, build 18.0.9598): ACTION_auto_bpm_transition implements onExecute and onQuery -> Dual; HTTP sweep classed it 'query'.
auto_bpm_transition.description: Gradually move BPM toward the other deck; an optional parameter forces which BPM it lands on

blink.name: blink
evidence: Kind from the vtable override matrix (tests/action-contracts.json, build 18.0.9598): ACTION_blink implements onQuery only -> Query; HTTP sweep classed it 'query'. Replaces the curated value 'Dual' (2026-09-15 normalisation).

2026-09-09, build 18.0.9583, HTTP query-only, waveform sampling at 20 Hz: an oscillator whose two arguments are both read. Position 1 (DUR) sets the period — 1000ms/500ms/2000ms measured 1.001/0.50/2.001 s — and position 2 (PCT) the duty cycle (25% -> ~0.28, 50% -> ~0.50, 75% untested). PCT is optional and defaults to ~50%. DUR takes beat units and those lock to the master tempo: blink 1bt and blink 500ms measured 0.467 s and 0.495 s in the same run at 129.44 BPM (1bt = 0.4635 s), so ms is absolute wall-clock and bt is not. Invisible to probe_arg_positions.py by construction — one query returns one sample of a square wave — so it is correctly disqualified there as drifting. Tracker: 'blink: An Oscillator, Tempo-Locked On Beat Units'.

Local test 2026-09-08, build 18.0.9598, HTTP channel, query position only. In query position the verb is a membership oracle for the sort-field enumeration: a real field answers no, anything else yes. 36 names separate from five agreeing nonsense controls and from plausible near-misses (play_count, date, added, random, folder, user1, user2, linkedvideo, hascue): album artist author bitrate bpm bpmdiff color comment composer drive field1 field2 filename filepath filesize firstplay firstseen genre grouping key keydiff label lastplay length order playcount pos position rating remix remixer stars title track type year. Exactly one leading + or - is accepted (++, *, ~ are not) and matching is case-insensitive. The boolean's MEANING is not established — the reading consistent with junk answering yes is that an unparsed key falls back to the current sort and so trivially matches it, which predicts a real key would answer yes once the browser is sorted by it; that prediction is untested because it needs an execute that has no readback to restore.

get_deck_analysis.name: get_deck_analysis

get_time.name: get_time
evidence: VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP, 2026-07-30): accepts a trailing argument — bare returns one time mode (286667) while ANY argument, including an unrecognized word, returns another (161780, matching 'elapsed'/'short'). Distinguishing 'short' from fallback needs value-format comparison; unknown args are silently defaulted, never E_INVALIDARG.

Local test 2026-09-06, HTTP, build 18.0.9598, known-position fixture (tests/get-time-positions.json, 2 runs x 2 phases, order varied). Position arguments discriminate against two nonsense controls and against each other: 'cue1' equals cue_pos 1 mseconly exactly and tracks the cue when it is moved; 'loopout' equals get_loop_out_time exactly; 'loopin' equals get_loop_in_time ONLY while a loop is active — with the loop exited it returns the loop-OUT value while the oracle still reports the in point. An unrecognized tail falls back to 'elapsed', NOT to the bare form (bare followed display_time 'remain' throughout), so bare-versus-argument separation is not recognition. 'short' alone behaves as an unrecognized tail. 'absolute' is a modifier, not a mode: it keeps the display_time setting. 'cue' reads the ACTIVE cue (0 until one is activated, then the active cue's position). 'to_lyrics' returned 0 with no lyrics — unresolved.

Local test 2026-09-06 (second pass, HTTP, build 18.0.9598), STRENGTHENING the same-day known-position result: 'absolute' is a pitch-removing modifier that keeps the display_time mode, now measured where the two timelines actually differ. At deck pitch +8.33% with the playhead fixed, get_time 'absolute' returned 55000 while 'remain' returned 50769 — and 55000 is exactly 90000 minus 35000, i.e. the REMAINING time computed on the unpitched 90 s timeline rather than the pitched 83076 ms one. The earlier run could not separate them because pitch was 0 there, which is why 'absolute' looked equal to 'remain'. get_time_sec 'absolute' agreed at 55.

Local test 2026-09-07, HTTP, build 18.0.9598, track with no lyrics on deck 1: get_time 'to_lyrics' returned 0 where a nonsense tail fell back to elapsed (44), so the tail is recognized even with nothing to report. Tracker: Documented Parameters Taken Live 2026-09-07 (second batch).

Local test 2026-09-12, HTTP, live get_build=9598, tests/long-time-forms.json (tools/probe_long_time.py). handshake.name: handshake
evidence: VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP, 2026-07-30): bare form returns E_INVALIDARG (argument required); 'handshake "nonce"' returns exactly 128 bytes of NON-UTF8 binary — a 1024-bit RSA block. Byte-identical for a repeated nonce (deterministic, so no random padding) and completely different for another nonce. Matches the bundled catalog description: a plugin passes any string, decrypts the result with VirtualDJ's handshake public key, and checks it matches. NOTE: reachable over the HTTP control channel, so that channel is a signing oracle for the handshake key — a shim host can proxy a plugin's challenge to a real VirtualDJ. See docs/Plugin SDK.md.

master_beat_num.name: master_beat_num
evidence: Verb table (arm64 slice, VirtualDJ 2026 bundle 18.0.9482, 2026-07-27): present, id 539, flags 256 (Button-Editor-hidden), category get. HTTP existence sweep 2026-07-27: exists, kind query.

VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP, 2026-07-30): BARE FORM RETURNS FLOAT BITS AS INT32 (type punning). Bare returns e.g. 1065869312 = 0x3f87e000; reinterpreting those bits as IEEE754 float32 gives 1.06, and successive samples decode to 1.06 -> 2.27 -> 3.49 -> 4.70, i.e. +1.21 beats per 0.6s, which matches the deck's live 118.66 BPM (1.98 beats/s) exactly. So the underlying value is a float beat counter rendered through an int path. With an argument the correct path is used: 'master_beat_num 5' returns 0.8. Hidden verb (flags==256).

Plugin channel (VDJIntrospect, VirtualDJ 2026 b18.0.9583, 2026-08-15): GetInfo returns S_OK with the double 1083943558.0 exactly — the float32 bit pattern 0x409baa86 (= 4.8646) reinterpreted as an integer. The defect is in the CORE, not HTTP rendering; consumers must reinterpret the int32 bits as float32.

param_cast.name: param_cast
evidence: Local test (HTTP query position, build 18.0.9598, 2026-09-07): a pipeline verb, so a chained expression is the whole state — no fixture needed. Through `get_var '$v' & param_cast <type>` with v=12.7: integer 13 and int_trunc 12 (the documented rounding-vs-truncation split, confirmed in one read), frac 0.7, '000' 013, percentage 1270%, ms 13ms, beats 12.7bt, float 12.7, text 12.7; boolean yes at 12.7 and no at 0. On a string source, 'text' 5 truncated 'Chapter & Verse' to 'Chapt' and 'text' 3 to 'Cha', so the optional character limit holds. Bare and two nonsense types raise E_INVALIDARG, as does 'artist' — that token is the doc example's argument to get_browsed_song, not a cast type. 'relative' and 'absolute' returned the input unchanged: they act on a slider parameter, which a query chain has none of, so they stay undiscriminated rather than refuted.

Local test 2026-09-08, build 18.0.9598, HTTP channel. param_cast REJECTS an unrecognized type (E_INVALIDARG) instead of ignoring it, so its vocabulary is directly enumerable by acceptance. 'absolute' and 'relative' are accepted and answer in a class of their own — '' where every cast type returns S_FALSE — matching the appendix's description that they change how the value is applied rather than casting it. Matching is exact, not prefix: 'int' and 'percent' are accepted, 'inte'/'integ'/'intx'/'perc'/'beat'/'abso' are not; the digit-format family generalises past the documented '000' to '0', '00', '0000' and '00.0'.

set.name: set
evidence: VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP interface, 2026-07-22): 'set $v on' stores yes and 'set $v off' stores no, but 'true'/'false' are NOT constants and store nothing. Quoting decides type: 5 and '5' are different values. Storing a string makes the variable unreadable and uncomparable — use numeric codes.

build 18.0.9598, HTTP, capture tests/variable-scope-probe-9598.json: variable scope prefixes are separate names and really isolate. A bare name is per-deck ('deck 1 set X 11' and 'deck 2 set X 22' read back 11 and 22); a $ name is shared across decks (set on deck 1, reads 33 from deck 2); bare/$/@ forms of one base name held 1/2/3 simultaneously. An unset name reads blank. Earlier: 'set $v on' stores yes and 'set $v off' stores no; string-valued variables are unsafe (see get_var, var_equal).

build 18.0.9598, HTTP, capture tests/variable-scope-probe-9598.json: '@' is a PERSISTENCE MODIFIER on the scope prefix, not a scope. Confirmed across a real restart: names left at 0 before a full quit came back as 0 for '@X' and blank for X, $X, #X, %X. '@X' is persistent AND deck-local (7 on deck 1, 8 on deck 2 at once); '@$X' is persistent AND global. Stored in settings.xml <VDJScriptGlobalVariables> as name=index=float with the '@' stripped, one row per deck for a deck-local name, written on quit.

settings.name: settings
evidence: Local test (HTTP, build 18.0.9598, 2026-09-08): in query position `settings '<page>'` answers whether the Settings dialog is currently showing that page — everything reads 'no' while the dialog is closed, so the vocabulary is only probeable with it open. With it open, the accepted pages are exactly the dialog's own nine tabs: audio, broadcast, controllers, extensions, interface, licenses, options, record, tutorials. Each selects itself (query yes) and drops the previous page to no; two nonsense controls and every unaccepted name leave the dialog where it was. Four of the nine (tutorials, interface, licenses, extensions) are absent from the binary's settings_pages table, and 14 of that table's members (all, automation, automix, browser, controls, internet, karaoke, modified, performance, sampler, skins, tags, timecode, video) are not accepted here — so that table is a different enumeration, not this verb's argument list. Two operational notes: opening the dialog STALLS the HTTP interface for several seconds (a timeout there is not a result), and it cannot be closed from script — bare `settings`, 'close' and 'off' all return false and leave it open; closing it took a click on the dialog's X, verified by the query returning to no.
